content.comment_body: Hello everyone, I'm new to this forum and to [product_name]. I'm working with Ubuntu Linux and experiencing connection problems with [product_name]. Both the device and my PC are on the same network and ping works in both directions. However, whenever I try to transfer data from the PC to [product_name], I get a persistent message saying the download failed. Oddly, if I place the PC on a different network (so they're not able to ping each other) and try transferring, the software can't find any devices, which is expected. I also tried on my Windows partition; everything installed successfully, but the software never starts. Many thanks in advance.

Which hardware version of [product_name] do you have? Is it the standard [product_name] or a newer version? Also, which version of the software are you using? Take a look at [url]: Why can't you download programs to your [product_name]?

I have the [article_no] version of [product_name] and I'm working with [product_name] software version [version_no]. I already tried with a third Windows PC and it works perfectly, but I'm still unable to connect using Linux.

Which hardware version of [product_name] do you have? Is it the standard or newer variant? What is the PC's IP address and subnet mask? What are the IP address and subnet mask of [product_name]? Are these addresses set to static?

Which hardware version do you have? Is it the standard [product_name] or a newer variant? What is the PC's IP address? 192.168.1.56 PC subnet mask? 255.255.255.0 Device IP address? 192.168.1.251 Device subnet mask? 255.255.255.0 Are IP addresses static? Yes. This setup works on Windows but not on Linux; shouldn't it be the same?
If the issue only occurs with Linux, check this [url]: Bug report regarding Java errors in [product_name] software for Linux. Specifically, review the post from [user_name] dated 12/13/2014.

Problem resolved! That post provided the solution. Only these commands were required: sudo mkdir -p /etc/sysconfig/network; sudo touch /etc/sysconfig/network/ifcfg-eth0; sudo touch /etc/sysconfig/network/ifcfg-wlan0.

Hello [user_name], I experienced the same issue while connecting to [product_name] using a USB cable. I currently use Linuxmint 19 and [product_name] software version [version_no]. Disabling my laptop's WiFi resolved the connectivity problem. Hopefully, this helps you as well!

Hello [user_name], Just a quick tip for connecting to [product_name] on a Linux computer: I encountered the same issue and found that turning off my laptop's WiFi solved it. I use Linuxmint 19 and [product_name] software version [version_no]. Hope this helps!

analysis.insight_summary: Several users are facing difficulties connecting [product_name] hardware to Linux PCs, especially when downloading programs via [product_name] software. The problem does not occur on Windows, indicating differences in cross-platform compatibility. Solutions include manual adjustment of network configuration files or disabling WiFi, suggesting that the software may lack optimized Linux-specific network management by default.
analysis.user_expectations: Users expect straightforward connectivity and programming access between [product_name] devices and Linux PCs using [product_name] software, without needing extra technical configuration. They hope for equivalent functionality between Windows and Linux versions.
